newsitem.title: THAILAND: ABN AMRO says confident of winning Thai bid.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO says confident of winning Thai bid.

text.p: ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia (Holdings) Ltd is confident a tender offer for Thai broker Asia Securities Trading will succeed, the bidder's managing director David Roberts said on Wednesday.
The firm announced a 35 baht per share offer for a 49 percent stake of the Thai broker on Wednesday. ABN AMRO said the purchase would cost some 2.2 billion baht ($80 million).

"We are highly confident that the deal will go through," Roberts told reporters, adding a failure to secure at least a 40 percent stake would endanger the whole deal, the offer for which closes on June 24.
"Today's events in the (equity) market shows the offer price is quite attractive, I think you can say we are quite confident," ABN AMRO country manager George Morgan said.

The Thai share market dropped 4.82 percent to end near an eight-year low on Wednesday on concerns over the Thai economy and its currency. Asia Securities' shares were suspended at the company's request on Wednesday morning at 24 baht per share.
ABN AMRO's offer to purchase the Thai broker was for long- term strategic reasons with a five- to 10-year focus, Morgan said.
Thailand's largest commercial bank Bangkok Bank Plc is a major shareholder in Asia Securities Trading with a 9.1 percent stake.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett expects to secure its stake in Asia Securities from smaller shareholders and wants Bangkok Bank to remain a major shareholder, Roberts and Morgan said.
Securities orders, which ABN AMRO Hoare Govett places on behalf of international clients through Asia Securities, account for about 40 of Asia Securities' total market share, Roberts said.
The bank hoped to expand Asia Securities' investment banking activities over the longer term, Roberts said.
No lay-offs were expected as the two firms' businesses are complementary, Roberts added.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia derives about 10 percent of its earnings in the region from its current activities in Thailand, Roberts said. ($1 = 26 baht)
